title: The notes-app battery on macOS: what it measures and which of it the public figures depend on
note: The plan for the run recorded in evidence/benchmarks/2026-08-16-notes-battery-macos.md,
written down after the fact from that note rather than before it -- said plainly here
because the point of frozen_at is that it precedes the run, and for this one it did not.
Later profiles are frozen first; this one is the existing measurement expressed in the
shape the audit can read, so its rejected energy leg stops being a sentence in a
document and becomes a cell that blocks a claim (IC-828).

cells.name: app-file-size
cells.definition: the app file itself, not its installed footprint

cells.name: memory-50k
cells.definition: resident memory with a 50,000-line document open, summed across processes

cells.name: warm-start-50k
cells.definition: time from launch to a visible window, second and later launches, 50,000 lines

cells.name: idle-cpu-50k
cells.definition: CPU with the document open and nothing happening, 50,000 lines

cells.name: scroll-pacing
cells.definition: p50 and p99 frame interval while scrolling; Krate only, no comparison instrument exists on macOS

cells.name: energy-scroll-leg
cells.definition: energy drawn over the scroll leg, from the platform power meter
